title: Union bound for restriction probabilities
statement:
Fix a parameter $p \in \bbr$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $A_0, \dots, A_{m-1}$ be finitely many events on restrictions of $n$ variables. Under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction, the probability that at least one of the events $A_i$ occurs is at most the sum of the probabilities of the individual events:
\[
  \bbP_p\!\left[\exists i,\ A_i(\rho)\right] \le \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} \bbP_p\!\left[A_i(\rho)\right],
\]
where $\bbP_p[\cdot]$ denotes the Bernoulli event probability at parameter $p$.
hypotheses_covered: finitely many events A_0, …, A_{m-1} on restrictions of n variables
replaced:
For $0\le p\le 1$ and finitely many events $A_0,\dots,A_{m-1}$ on restrictions, the
Bernoulli$(p)$ probability that some $A_i$ holds is at most the sum of the
individual probabilities:
\[
\mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,p\,(\exists i,\,A_i)\le
\sum_i \mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,p\,(A_i).
\]
